name: UK Overseas Territories Fund
summary: Collaborative funder round for environmental work in the UK Overseas Territories, covering practical conservation of land and marine habitats and species, plus capacity building and policy work. Grants run up to three years and can cover core costs.

steps: Stage 2 virtual follow-up meeting, if required

eligibility.rule: Is a UK charity working with a local Territory NGO, or a UKOT charity applying directly or via a UK conduit
Direct applicants from Anguilla, BVI, Montserrat or Turks and Caicos: led a Darwin Plus or EU BEST grant
NGOs registered only in the Falklands apply through a UK-registered charity
No capital developments or equipment, speculative land acquisition, one-off events or environmental education

documents: Most recent annual accounts, if a charity
Income and expenditure statement for department or unit, if part of a larger organisation
Brief explanation of significant surplus or deficit, or high or low reserves
Latest management accounts, if accounts year-end is more than 10 months old

applicant_types.quote: We welcome applications from UK charities working in partnership with local Territory-based NGOs and from charities based in the UKOTs.

geography.quote: We want to support transformative and locally-led change in the UKOTs through responsive environmental grantmaking.

places.quote: NGOs registered in Territories with UK-modelled charity governance systems (Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Gibraltar, and St Helena) will be able to apply directly.

eligibility.quote: We welcome applications from UK charities working in partnership with local Territory-based NGOs and from charities based in the UKOTs. UKOTs-based charities can apply either directly or through a conduit in the UK.

(Anguilla, British Virgin Islands, Montserrat, Turks & Caicos) will also be considered for direct funding. However, to ensure an extra level of compliance, NGOs from these Territories will be required to show evidence that they have been successfully accepted as the lead organisation on a UK Government Darwin Plus project grant or an EU BEST grant.
we will not accept direct funding requests from NGOs which are registered solely in the Falkland Islands, and will require applications to be made via a UK-registered charity.

documents.quote: All applicants are expected to submit a three-page proposal with supporting financial documents.

If you are a charity, a copy of your most recent annual accounts. If you are part of a larger organisation (such as a university) please provide an income and expenditure statement for the running costs of your department or unit, and explain how its funds are kept distinct from those of the wider institution.

If your accounts show a significant surplus or deficit, high or low reserves, please explain this briefly, including your policy on their future use/replenishment. If the year-end date of your accounts is more than 10 months old, please include your latest management accounts.
